layout_map:
1. Slide canvas — full-frame light gray field occupying nearly the entire 960×540 viewport
2. Frame border — thin dark hairline rectangle inset slightly from the canvas edges
3. Slide number badge — top-right corner, yellow circle with black "33"
4. Title — center of canvas, large red text "How to Kernelize SVM"
5. Cursor glyph — lower-left quadrant, small black arrow/pointer icon
6. Bottom strip — solid black horizontal bar along the bottom edge, roughly 8–10% of height
first_glance_test: Within 3 seconds a new user sees a title slide about SVM kernelization; the only readable content is the centered title and the small "33" slide counter. Actions offered: none visibly — no buttons, nav arrows, or interactive chrome; the screen is purely presentational. Focal point: the red centered title wins the eye immediately and correctly — it is the sole high-contrast element. Given the injected VIEW purpose (SVM/kernels/QP lecture frame), the title is the intended focal point and it does win the eye.
strengths: Title legibility: large centered red type on the light field is highly readable and instantly establishes the slide's subject.
Minimal composition: no visual noise competes with the title; the page is uncluttered.
Slide number placement: the top-right badge is visible but does not encroach on the title.

defects.description: slide canvas — full field — light-themed near-white canvas inside a dark-themed app context — breaks dark-mode surface elevation and reads as a jarring inversion — move embedded light content into a dark container or adopt a dark slide theme

bottom strip — bottom edge — heavy black horizontal bar along the bottom edge — unbalances the light canvas and reads like stray or clipped chrome rather than intentional slide design — remove or re-style the strip so it belongs to the canvas

frame border — bottom-right corner where it meets the bottom strip — unclear corner junction between the thin frame hairline and the black strip — reads as a broken or overlapping edge rather than a deliberate miter — verify the border-to-strip corner treatment

top_3: Section 4(g) — bottom black strip unbalances composition and reads as stray chrome.
Section 4(j) — frame-to-bottom-strip corner junction is unclear/possibly broken.
Section 4(a) — light-themed canvas inside a dark-themed app context risks a jarring surface inversion.
